angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 136,357 km at 56.70 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 17.6353 +/- 0.0492 mas (same row, RUWE 1.14): 56.70 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.196 +/- 0.006 solar radii from Niraula et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-315 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160..172N/abstract): 136,357 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.174 +/- 0.004 solar masses from Niraula et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-315 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160..172N/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3300 +/- 30 K from Niraula et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-315 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160..172N/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Niraula et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-315 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160..172N/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-315.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.094, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
